regime_classification.2026-04-10:growth: {"run_date":"2026-04-10","dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 56.5","signal_text":"PMI Composite at 56.5 flatters to deceive: Manufacturing PMI fell to 53.9 from 56.9, core sector decelerated to 2.3% from 4.7%, and airline passenger traffic dropped 9% to a 18-month low — none of which is consistent with a 7.8% economy firing on all cylinders. regime_classification.2026-04-10:inflation: {"run_date":"2026-04-10","dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 3.21%; Fuel -3.78%%","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 3.21% is benign, but the composition is a slow-motion trap: food inflation has jumped to 3.47% from 2.13% in a single print, FAO Food Index is at 128.5 (a 2.5% MoM rise), and Brent at $96.44 means the fuel deflation buffer of -3.78% is arithmetically finite — one administered price revision ends it. Core CPI is sticky at 3.4%, unchanged for two consecutive months, which tells you demand-side pricing power hasn't broken despite the rate cycle. Munger's inversion: if RBI cuts into a food-inflation re-acceleration while Brent adds $15bn to the import bill for every $10 move, the second-order effect is a CPI overshoot toward 5% by Q3 FY27 — precisely when the rate cut transmission would be peaking.","badge_label":"Within Band","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.2026-04-10:credit: {"run_date":"2026-04-10","dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 13.8%; CD 83.04%","signal_text":"CD ratio at 83.04% — the 81st percentile of its 10-year range — is the single most important number in today's dataset, and it is moving in the wrong direction from 82.5%. regime_classification.2026-04-10:policy: {"run_date":"2026-04-10","dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% with CPI at 3.21% implies a real policy rate of approximately +200bps — restrictive by India's historical standards, where neutral real rates have averaged 100-150bps.
